Hay celebraciones que podrían convertirse en rutina, pero Los Angeles Dodgers se niegan a tratarlas como algo normal. La franquicia volvió a apoderarse del título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional al derrotar 8-2 a los Cincinnati Reds en el Great American Ball Park. Fue su quinto campeonato divisional consecutivo y el número 13 en las últimas 14 temporadas, otra cifra que dimensiona el dominio de Los Ángeles en esta etapa.
King Tuck! pic.twitter.com/FGbgOZjXXS
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Kyle Tucker prendió la fiesta
La ofensiva encontró en Kyle Tucker a su principal protagonista. El jardinero terminó de 4 hits en 5 turnos, conectó un jonrón y produjo tres carreras, quedándose a un triple de completar el ciclo.
i love kyle tucker pic.twitter.com/ePeIAxm7re
— 🌱 jaime (@dodgersrpf) September 17, 2026
Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula y Miguel Rojas también impulsaron carreras para unos Dodgers que no necesitaron de un abridor tradicional. Justin Wrobleski trabajó tres entradas perfectas para iniciar un partido manejado desde el bullpen.
El triunfo dejó a Los Ángeles con marca de 93-60, nueve juegos por encima de los Padres de San Diego, que también ganaron durante la jornada pero ya no tenían forma matemática de alcanzar el liderato divisional.
Un dominio que parece no terminar
La dimensión del logro va mucho más allá de 2026.
Los Dodgers han conquistado el Oeste 13 veces durante sus últimas 14 campañas. La única excepción ocurrió en 2021, cuando los San Francisco Giants terminaron por delante de ellos.
Además, desde que MLB instauró el sistema divisional en 1969, Los Ángeles encabeza las Grandes Ligas con 24 campeonatos de división.
La franquicia también alcanzó su decimocuarta clasificación consecutiva a la postemporada, igualando la histórica racha de Atlanta entre 1991 y 2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
Muncy todavía disfruta el champán
Pese a estar acostumbrado a estas celebraciones, Max Muncy dejó claro que el momento conserva su valor.
“Nunca lo doy por sentado”, aseguró el veterano durante la celebración, destacando lo especial que resulta poder festejar después de atravesar una temporada de 162 partidos.
Y esta vez hubo razones de sobra para descorchar las botellas. Los Dodgers ya habían asegurado días antes su presencia en octubre, pero conquistar la división les permitió completar otro de los grandes objetivos de la temporada regular.
Ahora viene lo que realmente quieren
El título del Oeste, sin embargo, no representa la meta definitiva.
Los Dodgers llegan a octubre como campeones consecutivos de las Series Mundiales de 2024 y 2025 y persiguen algo que ningún equipo consigue desde los Yankees de Nueva York de 1998, 1999 y 2000: levantar tres Clásicos de Otoño consecutivos.
La corona divisional confirma que la maquinaria sigue funcionando. Ahora el reto será convertir nuevamente ese dominio de seis meses en victorias durante octubre.

Welcome to Waiver Wire Watch, our weekly fantasy baseball waiver wire guide. We’ll be doing things a little differently this season, with James Schiano publishing the initial waiver-wire article on Friday afternoon. Then Eric Samulski updates it every Sunday to make sure you get the most up-to-date information.
We’re doing things a little bit differently this time of year though. Rather than give a long list of players with deep analysis, there will only be a few dense player profiles for those we think currently need a bit more light shed on them. Otherwise, there will be long lists of players who can help your teams in a specific category or for this particular week.
The premise of the article is pretty straightforward. We’ll give you some recommended adds each week based on recent production or role changes. When we list a player, we’ll list the category where we think he’ll be helpful or the quick reason he’s listed. We hope this helps you determine whether the player fits your team’s needs. Not every “trending” player will be a good addition to your specific roster.
To qualify for this list, a player needs to be UNDER 40% rostered in Yahoo! formats. We understand you may say, “These players aren’t available in my league,” and we can’t help you there. These players are available in over 60% of leagues and some in 98% of leagues, so they’re available in many places, and that can hopefully satisfy readers who play in all league types.
⚾️Baseball is back on NBC: MLB returns to NBC and Peacock in 2026! In addition to becoming the exclusive home of Sunday Night Baseball, NBC Sports will broadcast MLB Sunday Leadoff, “Opening Day” and Labor Day primetime games, the first round of the MLB Draft, the entire Wild Card round of the postseason, and much more.
Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire Hitters
Jakob Marsee - OF, MIA (49% rostered)
(BATTING AVERAGE, OBP, COUNTING STATS PLAY)
Don’t let a dreadful start to the season distract you from how productive Marsee has been lately. Across nearly 200 plate appearances since the All-Star break, he’s slashing .287/.394/.482 with six home runs, 31 runs scored, and four stolen bases. Those four steals are a tad disappointing considering how often he ran last year and how often he’s gotten on base, but he’s a great source of hits and walks right now.
Victor Mesa Jr. - OF, TBR (26% rostered)
(POWER, SPEED, PLAYING TIME)
Mesa Jr. was activated off the injured list on September 1st after missing about two weeks with a hamstring strain and has gone right back to mashing. In 12 games since, he’s hitting .383 with three homers, 12 runs scored, eight RBI, and three stolen bases. He’s also sat three times, once against a right-handed pitcher (after playing consecutive days just off the IL) and twice against lefties. He’s also started against three lefties since, so he’s in a less stringent platoon than he was back in July and August. He’s been productive across the board whenever he’s played and could be reasonably relied upon in shallower leagues this week now with closer to a full-time role.
Josue De Paula - OF, LAD (12% rostered)
(HUGE PROSPECT PROMOTION, REAL POWER)
De Paula has held his own in one week of big league action with an .789 OPS across a measly 25 plate appearance sample entering play on Friday. That’s come in six starts – one of which against a left-handed pitcher – and he hit lead-off on Tuesday against a righty. He also sat in another game against a left-handed pitcher. In that small sample, we can see that he has plus bat speed to match his elite power pedigree. Also, he’s rarely chasing pitches out of the strike zone and making contact with the ones in it. He’s attempted two stolen bases too, but been caught once. This is all very encouraging after the 21-year-old left-handed slugger jumped straight from Double-A to the big leagues and may have the best offensive profile of any prospect in the minors. In 124 games this year with Tulsa, he hit 27 home runs and stole 31 bases with a .303/.401/.547 slash line. He also rarely struck out, took his walks, and can pull the ball in the air better than most other young players. Again, De Paula is as complete a hitter that we’ve seen called up to the majors recently.
Christian Encarnacion-Strand - 1B/3B, BAL (10% rostered)
(POWER, POST HYPE BREAKOUT?)
Encarnacion-Strand has enjoyed a late season renaissance since joining the Orioles. In 51 games, he has 10 home runs, 12 doubles, and an .846 OPS. That’s come with excellent power metrics like a 15.3% barrel rate and 73.6 mph bat speed. His hit tool and overall swing decisions remain concerning, but he’s a very legitimate power threat right now while he’s consistently putting his bat on the ball.
Leo Bernal - C, STL (3% rostered)
(PROSPECT PROMOTION, HOT STREAK)
The Cardinals promoted Bernal on September 1st when the rosters expanded and he’s started all 15 games since going 18-for-61 with three home runs, three doubles, and 15 RBI. He’s started 13 games at catcher, four at designated hitter, and one at first base over that span, so it’s clear the Cardinals are doing everything they can to get his bat in the lineup everyday. A switch-hitter with real power from each side of the plate, Bernal had 16 home runs, nine stolen bases, and a 115 wRC+ through 101 games at Triple-A this season as a 22-year-old with a strong underlying profile to match. He’s a great play in deep mixed or two-catcher leagues at the moment.
Emmanual Rodríguez - OF, MIN (2% rostered)
(PROSPECT CALL-UP, POSSIBLE POWER UPSIDE)
Rodríguez put together a solid first week in the big leagues going 5-for-23 with a home run, double, and triple. That’s come with a very high average bat speed at 77.1 mph – the same as Kyle Schwarber – but has struck out in one third of his plate appearances so far. He’s started all six games too and jumped up as high as fifth in the Twins’ order on Thursday. Rodríguez slashed .262/.414/.500 with 11 homers, 33 RBI, 36 runs scored, and seven steals across 220 Triple-A plate appearances this year, and, much like Walker Jenkins, could have been called up sooner had it not been for injuries. He rarely chases pitches out of the zone and makes plenty of hard contact, which is a combination we like. Considering he’s likely going to play a bunch and has real power, he could offer a spark this week.

Fantasy Baseball Waiver Wire Pitchers
Emmet Sheehan - SP, LAD (53% rostered)
Blake Snell was removed from his start on Wednesday after one inning with left groin tightness. So, the recently optioned Sheehan might get another chance in the Dodgers’ rotation next week. Shuttled up and down a couple times recently, Sheehan returned to the big leagues for two starts after spending most of August in Triple-A and struck out 15 batters over two starts spanning 11 2/3 innings with just one earned run. He showed a renewed confidence in his fastball and that pitch was missing bats. Again, this is more speculative as Snell’s removal from his start appeared to be at least partially precautionary, but Sheehan could start at home against the Padres next week.
Justin Wrobleski - SP/RP LAD (41% rostered)
A pitcher’s upcoming schedule can be more important than their skill this time of year and Wrobleski is scheduled to face the Rafael Devers-less Giants twice to close the season. Bailey Ober and Zebby Matthews are also streaming options against the Giants. Overall, these are not a trio of pitchers we’d be running to recommend besides for this particular matchup.
Ryan Johnson - SP/RP, LAA (22% rostered)
As the Angels have overhauled their organizational pitching structure, many of their arms have made key adjustments over the last month. Johnson is part of that group, mostly trashing his sinker starting on August 11th. Since then, he has a 2.04 ERA across 39 2/3 innings. It’s still not a great profile – he’s a sidearming righty who doesn’t miss many bats and rarely throws a pitch over 90 mph besides that sinker – but he has a strong cutter, sweeper, and splitter. He’s scheduled to close the season with outings against the Twins and Mariners as a risky streaming option with good results lately.
Andrew Alvarez - SP/RP, WSN (22% rostered)
Alvarez is coming off a gem against the Angels last Saturday with a career-high seven scoreless innings, eight strikeouts, and just one hit allowed. He also walked four batters. In that game, the Angels ran out a lineup with nine right-handed hitters against the left-handed Alvarez and he tore through them with his curveball. His best pitch, it forced 10 of his 15 total whiffs and set up his auxiliary fastball and slider to get called strikes because hitters were so keyed in on the hook. His fastball leaves plenty to be desired at 92 mph with a suboptimal shape, but his curve and slider have a uniquely symbiotic relationship. David Laurila wrote about this on FanGraphs a few months back in an interview with Alvarez. Those two pitches have practically the same velocity and spin axis while the curveball has significantly more depth making hitters struggle to decipher between the two. He’s mildly trustworthy on Saturday against the Cardinals and again against the Mets next weekend.
Jonah Tong - SP, NYM (14% rostered)
Tong turned in another solid start on Monday against the Orioles going six strong with six strikeouts, one walk, and one unearned run. He pushed up his fastball usage heavily in this outing compared to his last, jumping up from 31% to 55% as he found a little bit of extra life on it. That could’ve been weather related as there was a brisk headwind in Citi Field that night – which can help pitchers add a bit of induced vertical break on their fastballs – but it was still the out-pitch Tong had envisioned. Off that dominant fastball, he was able to sequence his changeup, cutter, and curveball more effectively than he has otherwise against major league hitters and looked good overall. He has a huge test against the Phillies this Sunday to try and keep the momentum going before facing the Nationals next week to close the season.
Anthony Molina - RP/SP, SFG (5% rostered)
After being ripped for seven runs by the Padres last week, Molina bounced back well with 5 2/3 scoreless innings and six strikeouts on Tuesday against the Cardinals. He had much better command of his fastball in that more recent outing and that’s important for Molina because while that pitch has plus velocity around 96 mph, its shape is mediocre. So, it needs to be commanded in order to be consistently effective. Otherwise, that pitch is flanked by a quality curveball that’s effective against hitters from both sides of the plate, a solid slider, and a changeup that can miss bats against lefties. He’s scheduled to face the Twins at home next week to close his season.

item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- Heralded by the thumping beat of "Bailalo Rocky," Roki Sasaki opened eyes and electrified Chavez Ravine as the postseason closer during the Dodgers' run to back-to-back championships. The 24-year-old could be poised for a return to the 'pen for L.A.'s three-peat bid -- but he'll make at least one more start before the end of the regular season.
Sasaki has been sidelined since exiting his Aug. 26 start in Atlanta due to a blister on his right middle finger, and he should be activated from the 15-day injured list during the Dodgers' final homestand, likely in next week's series against the Padres.
The Dodgers had been considering getting Sasaki reacclimated to the bullpen before the postseason, but they kept the option of him starting open. Sasaki has remained stretched out during his time on the IL, most recently throwing four simulated innings on 48 pitches on Wednesday afternoon in Cincinnati.
"There's benefits both ways," manager Dave Roberts said. "One can argue it's best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up. Because if something does happen, he's built up. The other side is you can assimilate him into the 'pen and get comfortable in that role -- if that is the role. And so again, that's why we have to be really thoughtful with that."
On Wednesday night, the benefit of having additional rotation depth in Sasaki became clear when Blake Snell exited his start against the Reds after just one inning due to left groin tightness. Removing him from the game was seen as more of a precautionary move, but it exposed the somewhat tenuous state of the Dodgers' starting pitching at present.
If the projected postseason rotation of Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Snell and Tyler Glasnow remain healthy, then the Dodgers will be in a great place. But there are question marks behind the Big Four. Shohei Ohtani will not pitch again this season. Justin Wrobleski moved to the bullpen and has been much shakier in the second half. Emmet Sheehan, who's currently with Triple-A Oklahoma City, is trending upward after his two most recent starts in the Majors -- but has been inconsistent overall.
Yamamoto is the only member of L.A.'s rotation who has not missed a start this season. Both Skubal and Snell had surgery to remove loose bodies from their left elbows. Glasnow spent more than three months on the IL due to lower back spasms, a recurring issue for him. The Dodgers have been proactive with managing Glasnow's back, as Roberts said he flew back to L.A. early to cut out an additional flight segment in between last Saturday's start in Miami and his next scheduled start on Friday.
Should anything happen to those four, Sasaki would figure to be the next arm up in the rotation. Sasaki has broken out in his second Major League season, even though his 5-5 record and 4.60 ERA may seem underwhelming at first glance. After a shaky start to the campaign, Sasaki introduced a new splitter and began to consistently throw his fastball harder, helping him achieve sustainable success as a starter. He posted a 2.63 ERA in seven starts before the blister issue arose.
Because Sasaki is returning from an injury, there may be some rust for him to knock off. He is still pitching with the blister, but Roberts said he felt good after covering it with Dermabond in his most recent bullpen session and simulated game.
"It's playable," Roberts said. "Given the Dermabond, the time that he'll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it's dang near close to being healed."
The Dodgers expect Sasaki to play an important role on their postseason pitching staff, even though they're not sure which role he'll fulfill -- but it is easier to shorten him up to pitch in relief rather than have to build him back up to start. After the latest injury concern, opting to keep starting on the table for Sasaki has already proven wise.

CINCINNATI -- Try as they might to view 2026 as its own season, everything the Dodgers have done this year is impossible to separate from the larger context of what they have accomplished in more than a decade of excellence.
The Dodgers hit another key milestone in their title defense by reclaiming the NL West crown with an 8-2 victory over the Reds on Thursday afternoon at Great American Ball Park. Three days after their traditional champagne toast in honor of clinching a postseason berth, winning the West brought on a wild clubhouse celebration -- which they hope will be the first of many over the next several weeks.
"You get so mired in each year, it’s hard to have any perspective," president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman said. "We’ve had our share of troubles this year. Things where we had to work harder than we expected on a couple of fronts. But the important thing is how we finish and how we go into October."
In their record-tying 14 consecutive postseason appearances, the Dodgers have 13 division titles. The only team to unseat them was the 2021 Giants, who edged them in one of the most highly contested NL West races in recent memory.
Since divisional play began in 1969, the Dodgers lead all big league teams with 24 division titles, one more than the Braves -- currently in line to win the NL East -- and three more than the Yankees. Each year's achievements raise the bar for every ensuing year. The expectations facing the Dodgers have become nearly impossible to meet. But they've embraced them gladly.
"There is certainly a higher expectation when, if you don't win the World Series, you fail," manager Dave Roberts said. "But that's kind of part of what you signed up with the Dodgers.”
The Dodgers' offense, whose inconsistency has been a perpetual concern over the course of the season, provided plenty of early support to back a scheduled bullpen game. Kyle Tucker led the way with a four-hit, three-RBI showing, finishing a triple shy of the Dodgers’ first cycle since 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, Josue De Paula and Miguel Rojas also knocked in runs.
Justin Wrobleski opened the bullpen game with three perfect innings, and while Blake Treinen surrendered a solo home run in the fourth, Landon Knack pitched four scoreless frames before Seth Halvorsen allowed a run in the ninth.
With nine games remaining in the regular season, the Dodgers are far from full strength. Their best hitter, Shohei Ohtani, is on the 15-day IL, as is first-time All-Star Andy Pages. The six-man rotation they carried for most of the season has been reduced to four fully stretched-out starters on the active roster, necessitating Thursday's bullpen game.
"It's been the same thing the last couple years," Muncy said. "We've had guys go down. We've had guys step up in their place. … That's all that we ask, and we've been able to survive a lot."
The Dodgers are expecting reinforcements back before the postseason, and would greatly benefit from securing a first-round bye to advance directly to the NL Division Series -- giving them five days off after the end of the regular season. They hold a four-game lead over the Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League.
This edition of the Dodgers is not without its flaws, but then again, neither were the back-to-back champion teams in 2024 and '25. After becoming the first team in a quarter-century to defend their title last year, they will vie for the Majors' first three-peat since the 1998-2000 Yankees.
While the talk of a three-peat began almost from the moment the Dodgers became back-to-back champions last November, Roberts urged his team to stay focused on the present while keeping the larger goal in mind. In his annual speech on the first day of full-squad workouts during Spring Training, he delivered the following message: Be a greyhound, looking forward with blinders on.
Tarik Skubal was not a Dodger when Roberts gave his spring address, but he saw the message play out after he was dealt to L.A. ahead of the Trade Deadline. He arrived at the beginning of a season-high seven-game losing streak -- and the tough stretch gave him a feel for the culture that has led to his new team's sustained success.
"I think there was no panic from this group," Skubal said. "I think that’s why in big moments, pressure doesn't really get to these guys."
The Dodgers have a long road ahead as they look to get back to the World Series, but it bears similarities to the roads they have traveled before. The slate might be wiped clean every year, but they have experience weathering the challenges along the way to the promised land.
"It's a different year, but I think it's kind of the same," Mookie Betts said. "The same group of guys. We know what to expect. We know what to expect from each other. It's the same goal every year. Getting here, you can't really get too focused on how, as long as you get there."

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers were already playoff-bound for the 14th straight season. But after taking down the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, they're winners of the NL West for the 13th time in that span and for the fifth season in a row.
Of course, the streak LA cares about most will be at stake in the postseason. The Dodgers are aiming to become the first team to three-peat as World Series champions since the fabled New York Yankees of 1998-2000.
With the victory Thursday, the Dodgers (93-60) have the second-best record in the NL, behind only the Milwaukee Brewers (95-58), who clinched the NL Central earlier this week but dropped their series finale to the Pirates on Thursday. The Dodgers and Brewers will jockey for the NL's top seed over the final week of the regular season.
Meanwhile, LA will do its best to sort out an injury-riddled roster before the calendar flips to October. Most notably, the status of Shohei Ohtani will be acutely monitored, as the two-way star has been juggling issues with his biceps, left knee and neck.
Then there's lefty starting pitcher Blake Snell, who's dealing with a groin injury that ended his start Wednesday versus the Reds after just one inning.
Andy Pages is expected back in the Dodgers' outfield soon. However, only time will tell how quickly he returns to form after healing from a fractured left hand.
A bullpen game and a flurry of early scoring sealed the NL West in Cincy
LA didn't need one of its aces to secure the division title on Thursday. Manager Dave Roberts, who has overseen 10 of the Dodgers' NL West crowns amid this memorable run, opted for a bullpen game.
Lefty Justin Wrobleski spun three innings of shutout ball. He was the first to punch out Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, who clocked out with three Ks on the day. Cincinnati's lone run came in the fourth, when Sal Stewart homered off Dodgers right-handed hurler Blake Treinen.
Then righty Landon Knack registered four scoreless innings while allowing four hits. Seth Halvorsen finished the game while allowing one more Reds run to score in the ninth.
That merely made a dent in LA's commanding lead. The Dodgers built that in large part thanks to a trio of extra-base hits. Kyle Tucker went yard in the first inning, depositing a two-run dinger. He also hit an RBI double in the second. In the fourth, Max Muncy drove home a pair of runs with a two-bagger.
The Reds and Dodgers traded runs in the ninth, with Miguel Rojas taking one deep to put the exclamation point on LA's division-clinching victory.

item.content:encoded:
Lo que hace de Shohei Ohtani el jugador más extraordinario en la historia de MLB podría ser también su único defecto fatal.
A diferencia de cualquier jugador que haya existido antes que él, Ohtani puede dominar en el plato y en el montículo, pero ha llegado el momento de decidir si lanzar vale la pena por el desgaste que ha provocado en su cuerpo.
Te puede interesar: La decisión de los Dodgers de descansar a Shohei Ohtani como pitcher es la correcta
Los Dodgers colocaron a Ohtani en la lista de lesionados la semana pasada debido a lesiones en la rodilla y el bíceps que han persistido durante meses. Los problemas de rodilla comenzaron oficialmente el 11 de junio, mientras que el problema en el bíceps existe desde algún momento de mayo. No ha realizado una apertura desde el 3 de julio y cada vez que intentaba aumentar su carga de trabajo para regresar, el problema de rodilla generaba un estrés adicional en el bíceps, frenando su progreso. Es muy poco probable que vuelva a subir al montículo esta temporada.
Francamente, no deberíamos volver a verlo lanzar.
Sería una decisión difícil, por decir lo menos. En 14 aperturas esta temporada, Ohtani ha sido dominante. Tiene marca de 8–2, con efectividad de 1.79, WHIP de 0.95 y 95 strikeouts contra 26 bases por bolas en 85 ⅔ innings. Generó 2.9 fWAR como pitcher esta temporada, su mayor cifra desde 2022, cuando realizó 28 aperturas, la mayor cantidad de su carrera. Se nos ha recordado la increíble capacidad que lo convirtió en la primera auténtica estrella de dos vías de este deporte. Desafortunadamente, mantener esa capacidad ha tenido un costo en repetidas ocasiones.
Ohtani ha sufrido una larga lista de lesiones a lo largo de los años mientras intentaba ser un pitcher abridor de tiempo completo y un bateador de todos los días. Esos esfuerzos anteriormente no habían afectado sus capacidades en el plato, pero ahora que tiene 32 años, parece que eso ha comenzado a suceder.
Ohtani ha estado intentando regresar al montículo desde aquella apertura del 3 de julio y su producción como bateador ha disminuido desde entonces. En 49 partidos, registra una línea ofensiva de .259/.342/.518, con 12 home runs, 30 carreras impulsadas y un wRC+ de 127. La mayoría de los demás jugadores de MLB estarían encantados con esos resultados, pero su OPS de .860 durante ese periodo está muy por debajo de las marcas superiores a 1.000 que registró en cada una de las tres temporadas anteriores. Su wRC+ en ese periodo sería el más bajo desde 2020 y casi 50 puntos menor que el de la temporada pasada (172). La lesión de rodilla también ha limitado la velocidad que lo ayudó a robar 59 bases hace dos años. Este año solo suma 11 en 14 intentos.
Las lesiones relacionadas con el pitcheo ya se estaban acumulando durante las primeras temporadas de Ohtani en Estados Unidos. Después de 10 aperturas en 2018, sufrió un desgarro del ligamento colateral ulnar de su brazo derecho y necesitó una cirugía Tommy John. No lanzó en absoluto en 2019 y, cuando regresó al año siguiente, sufrió una distensión del flexor después de dos aperturas y no volvió a lanzar.
En 2021 y 2022 estuvo mayormente saludable y realizó 51 aperturas combinadas sin problemas importantes. A eso le siguieron 23 aperturas en 2023 antes de volver a sufrir un desgarro del UCL y someterse a su segunda cirugía importante de codo en cinco años. No lanzó al año siguiente y regresó al montículo después de casi dos años en 2025, cuando lanzó 47 innings en 14 aperturas. Esta temporada, ni siquiera llegó a los 90 innings antes de volver a ser apartado.
Ohtani está en su novena temporada en MLB y ha lanzado 614 ⅓ innings en su carrera; 428 ⅓ llegaron durante un periodo de tres años entre 2021 y 2023. Eso significa que casi 70% de sus innings de carrera se produjeron durante esas tres temporadas. En sus otras seis campañas combinadas, solo ha lanzado 186 innings.
Cuando Ohtani no está en el montículo, sigue siendo uno de los dos bateadores más valiosos del planeta, junto con Aaron Judge. Cuando está saludable, destroza a los pitchers rivales. Ganó un MVP en 2024 sin lanzar un solo pitch y volvió a ganarlo en 2025 a pesar de lanzar apenas 47 innings. ¿La lección? No necesita estar en el montículo para ser uno de los mejores jugadores del beisbol.
A medida que envejece, el desgaste físico de continuar lanzando se vuelve cada vez más difícil de justificar. Esta temporada es simplemente el ejemplo más reciente. Sigue siendo un jugador de nivel All-Star, pero no ha sido sobrehumano. Los Dodgers no le pagaron $700 millones para ver cómo su mayor habilidad se deteriora mientras persigue inútilmente más innings.
Ohtani lanzó a nivel de as esta temporada cuando estuvo en el montículo y, de haber mantenido ese ritmo, habría estado en la pelea por el Cy Young de la Liga Nacional. En lugar de perseguir un nuevo reconocimiento, el cuatro veces MVP ahora está en la lista de lesionados mientras se acercan los playoffs. Es la misma historia que hemos visto una y otra vez, con pequeñas variaciones, desde que debutó en MLB. Las exigencias físicas de ser tanto pitcher abridor como bateador de todos los días simplemente podrían ser demasiado para que su cuerpo las soporte.
A estas alturas, la única solución es que Ohtani deje de lanzar y se concentre en ser bateador. Incluso si los Dodgers encontraran de alguna manera la forma de reducir su carga de trabajo como pitcher, todavía tendría que prepararse como lanzador todos los días. Ohtani tendría que realizar sesiones de bullpen, mantener su programa habitual de pitcheo y preparar su codo derecho, operado quirúrgicamente en dos ocasiones, para lanzar a 100 mph cada pocos días. Esa es la carga que repetidamente ha descarrilado su carrera como pitcher.
Los Dodgers no necesitan que Ohtani lance. Tienen una rotación repleta de talento encabezada por Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow y, por el momento, Tarik Skubal. Snell y Glasnow han tenido problemas para mantenerse en el montículo, pero ambos tienen contrato al menos hasta la próxima temporada. Mientras tanto, jugadores como Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan y Roki Sasaki proporcionan profundidad adicional para la rotación. El pitcheo de Ohtani es un lujo del que Los Angeles puede darse el lujo de prescindir.
Durante años, Ohtani ha maravillado al beisbol con sus enormes home runs, velocidades de salida de otro mundo y actuaciones ofensivas que el juego nunca había visto antes. Su capacidad para lanzar lo hizo único, pero ya no vale la pena correr el riesgo. Su experimento de dos vías fue una de las hazañas más impresionantes en la historia del deporte. Continuarlo no vale la pena si eso significa perder la magia que puede crear con un bat en las manos.
En el plato, Ohtani es un superhéroe. En el montículo, es frágil. Ya no tiene sentido arriesgar al Ohtani bateador por tener la posibilidad de contar con el Ohtani pitcher.
Ohtani podría ser el Ícaro del beisbol. Aquello que lo hizo milagroso podría terminar siendo lo que lo haga volver a tocar tierra.
La diferencia es que Ohtani puede alejarse de su defecto fatal antes de que se convierta en su caída.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers clinched the NL West for the 14th time in their last 15 seasons with an 8-2 win over the Cincinnati Reds on Thursday. Justin Wrobleski pitched three perfect innings, Freddie Freeman continued to heat up, Miguel Rojas hit just his fourth homer of the year, but the Dodgers' top performer, not just in the series finale, but over the Dodgers' last 10 games was Kyle Tucker.
He homered in his first at-bat on Thursday to give the Dodgers an early 2-0 lead. By the end of the game, he'd gone 4-for-5 with the homer, two doubles, three RBI, and ended up a triple shy of the cycle.
After a long season of struggles and fans and writers alike wondering aloud if the Dodgers made a huge mistake signing him to his absurd four-year, $240 million contract, Tucker seems to have turned back into his old self at just the right time.
The Dodgers, while still heavy favorites to win the World Series, have a whole host of weaknesses their upcoming postseason opponents can (and will) identify and exploit. But Tucker earning back his old King Tuck moniker in LA would add an extra bite the lineup expected but hasn't seen most of this season.
However, there's a caveat to all of this that Dodgers fans shouldn't ignore. LA has played seven of their last 10 games against the Reds, one of the worst teams in the National League.
Kyle Tucker's newfound success for the Dodgers has to be tempered by one unavoidable fact
Before coming into this nine-game stretch, Tucker hit .143 with a .628 OPS against the Detroit Tigers, St. Louis Cardinals, and Washington Nationals. All are inferior opponents to the Dodgers and some even had worse records than the Reds by the time they saw the Dodgers. But none had the NL or AL's second-worst run differential like Cincinnati.
Going into this series, Cincinnati had a staggering -148 run differential. Their pitching staff's collective ERA is 4.87 and WHIP is 1.45, the third-worst in baseball in both categories. Of the four starters the Dodgers faced during this series, only Andrew Abbott had an ERA under 5.00 (4.78).
The Dodgers' last nine games should be a greater test of Tucker's mettle, and will prove whether or not this hot streak was purely incidental. Six inter-division games against the San Francisco Giants and three against the San Diego Padres are surely going to give the Dodgers more grief, as games against those teams often do, and may expose this recent surge as being nothing more than a flash in the pan.

Los Dodgers reconquistan el Oeste de la Liga Nacional y sellan su 14ª postemporada consecutiva
CINCINNATI._ Por más que intenten ver el 2026 como una temporada independiente, todo lo que los Dodgers han hecho este año es imposible de separar del contexto más amplio de lo que han logrado en más de una década de excelencia.
Catorce clasificaciones consecutivas a la postemporada. Cinco títulos divisionales seguidos. La inusual oportunidad de luchar por un tricampeonato de la Serie Mundial.
Los Dodgers alcanzaron otro hito importante en la defensa de su título al recuperar la corona del Oeste de la Liga Nacional con una victoria de 8-2 sobre los Rojos la tarde del jueves en el Great American Ball Park. Tres días después de su tradicional brindis con champaña para celebrar que aseguraron un lugar en la postemporada, conquistar el Oeste desató una eufórica celebración en el clubhouse, que esperan sea la primera de muchas durante las próximas semanas.
En sus 14 participaciones consecutivas en la postemporada, igualando un récord, los Dodgers han conquistado 13 títulos divisionales. El único equipo que logró destronarlos fueron los Gigantes del 2021, que los superaron por estrecho margen en una de las luchas por el Oeste de la Liga Nacional más reñidas de los últimos tiempos.
La ofensiva de los Dodgers, cuya inconsistencia ha sido una preocupación constante a lo largo de la temporada, brindó bastante respaldo desde temprano para apoyar un juego de bullpen programado. Kyle Tucker encabezó el ataque con cuatro hits y tres carreras impulsadas, quedándose a un triple de conseguir el primer ciclo de los Dodgers desde el 2017. Freddie Freeman, Max Muncy, el dominicano Josué De Paula y el venezolano Miguel Rojas también remolcaron anotaciones.
Justin Wrobleski abrió el juego de bullpen con tres innings perfectos, y aunque Blake Treinen permitió un jonrón solitario en el cuarto episodio, Landon Knack lanzó cuatro entradas en blanco antes de que Seth Halvorsen concediera una rayita en el noveno acto.
Con nueve juegos restantes en la temporada regular, los Dodgers están lejos de contar con todo su plantel. Su mejor bateador, Shohei Ohtani, está en la lista de lesionados de 15 días, al igual que el cubano Andy Pagés, llamado por primera vez al Juego de Estrellas. La rotación de seis abridores que utilizaron durante gran parte de la temporada se ha reducido a cuatro abridores completamente acondicionados en el róster activo, lo que hizo necesario recurrir a un juego de bullpen el jueves.
Los Dodgers esperan recuperar refuerzos antes de la postemporada y se beneficiarían enormemente de asegurar el descanso en la primera ronda para avanzar directamente a la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional, lo que les daría cinco días libres después del final de la temporada regular. Tienen una ventaja de 4.0 juegos sobre los Bravos por el segundo puesto de la Liga Nacional.
Esta versión de los Dodgers no está exenta de defectos, pero tampoco lo estuvieron los equipos campeones consecutivos del 2024 y 2025. Después de convertirse el año pasado en el primer equipo en un cuarto de siglo en defender con éxito su título, buscarán el primer tricampeonato de Grandes Ligas desde los Yanquis de 1998 al 2000.
“Tenemos tanta hambre como en el 2024 y 2025”, dijo el piloto Dave Roberts. “Esta es una temporada aparte. Nuestros muchachos lo entienden”.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Cincinnati Reds 8-2 on Thursday, September 17th, to clinch the National League West.
Kyle Tucker’s big day
Tucker has been fantastic lately, and Thursday’s game was a true cherry on top. He went 4-for-5 with two doubles, a home run, and a single, and drove in three runs.
Over the last seven games, Tucker has put up a .375/.467/.917 slash line with three home runs, nine RBIs, five walks, and three strikeouts.
Even over the last 15 games, Tucker is hitting .280/.383/.680 with five home runs and 11 RBIs.
Tucker nearly had a cycle, but when he gapped a ball in the eighth inning, he didn’t push for a triple and held up instead.
Still, this was Tucker’s game and a promising sign of things to come.
It was not just Tucker who played well, though; Freddie Freeman went 2-for-3 with an RBI and a walk, while Max Muncy went 2-for-4 with two RBIs.
Additionally, Miguel Rojas added the eighth run with a solo home run in the top of the ninth.
Considering the Dodgers went 0-for-11 with runners in scoring position on Wednesday, Thursday’s game was a welcome development.
Bullpen bounce-back
Justin Wrobleski looked great for three innings, allowing no hits and pitching them all perfect, with three strikeouts.
He was only at 32 pitches, and if Roberts wanted to stretch him out, he could have, but the Dodgers want to save his best stuff for the postseason.
Additionally, Landon Knack handled the bulk of the relief, allowing just four hits and recording two punchouts over four innings of clean work.
Blake Treinen and Seth Halvorsen each allowed a run, but thanks to Knack and Wrobleski, it was more than enough to finally clinch the division.

CINCINNATI — There is the road less traveled. And there is what the Dodgers do every year.
For the 13th time in the past 14 years, they are the National League West division champions. They clinched it with an 8-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds Thursday afternoon.
The Dodgers scored seven times in the first four innings, leaving little doubt about the outcome.
There was little doubt about this year’s division title either.
The Dodgers spent a total of six days out of first place this season – two in April, four in May. They took over first place for good after beating the San Diego Padres on May 19. They had a double-digit lead for the first time on June 28 and have led by no less than seven games every day since.
Any drama is quickly draining from the playoff seeding race as well. Thursday’s win put the Dodgers four games up on the Atlanta Braves (off on Thursday) with a magic number of six to clinch one of the top two seeds and a first-round bye.
Clinching a postseason berth for the 14th consecutive season (tying the Braves’ MLB record) on Monday required only a champagne toast and a short speech from Dodgers manager Dave Roberts.
“This is kind of the expectation,” veteran Max Muncy said of that. “It’s not something you take for granted, but it’s the expectation that you can reach this point every single year.”
Clinching another division title, however, did not get the low-key treatment. The team celebrated in earnest.
No one had more reason to wash away the regular season and focus on the postseason than Kyle Tucker. The offseason’s big signing, Tucker has been a disappointment, making his four-year, $240 million contract stand out as the kind of mistake only the Dodgers could absorb.
But Tucker has shown signs of life recently.
He drove in the Dodgers’ first two runs Thursday with a first-inning home run, had an RBI double in the second inning, singled and scored a run in the fourth. With a shot at the cycle, he flew out in the fifth then doubled again in the eighth. Over his past eight games, Tucker is 12 for 29 (.414) with three doubles, a triple and four home runs.
Muncy had a two-run double in the fourth inning and Freddie Freeman went 2 for 3 with two runs scored and a sacrifice fly. Miguel Rojas hit a solo home run in the ninth.
The early lead made the bullpen game a smooth ride. Justin Wrobleski started and retired all nine batters he faced. Blake Treinen gave up a solo home run to Sal Stewart in the fourth inning. But Landon Knack followed that with four scoreless innings.

item.content:encoded:
Earlier this week after Monday’s 4-1 road victory against the Cincinnati Reds, the Los Angeles Dodgers clinched a playoff berth for the fourteenth consecutive season, an all-time record that ties them with the Atlanta Braves who accomplished it from 1991 to 2005.
A large part of the Dodgers’s success this season has been how good their starting rotation has been. The team has an enormous amount of pitching depth which means they are constantly sending elite starting pitchers to the bump day-in-and-out.
| ERA | WHIP | BB/9 | K/9 |
| 3.45 (2nd) | 1.09 (2nd) | 2.57 (3rd) | 9.19 (4th) |
When I said that the Dodgers have an enormous amount of starting pitching depth, I really did mean a ton of depth.
Their active starting rotation currently consists of Tyler Glasnow, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Yoshinobu Yamamoto, but they also have Justin Wrobleski down in the bullpen who put up an excellent first-half in the starting rotation.
You’d think that’s a pretty good rotation by itself and it certainly is, but they have plenty more quality arms remain either in the minors or on the injured list. These names include: Kris Bubic, Landon Knack, Eric Lauer, Roki Sasaki, Emmet Shehaan, Gavin Stone and of course, Shohei Ohtani.
That right there is enough talent to construct two top-10 starting rotations in the majors, which is incredible. The Dodgers’ plethora of depth is great, but it brings us to an interesting discussion.
The Dodgers coaching staff will have a large selection of elite arms to choose from to open up Postseason action, but who is the most logical and realistic starting pitcher for Game 1?
All stats updated prior to games on Thursday, September 17
Blake Snell, LHP
Snell has pitched really well since returning to the starting rotation in early August. Injuries have kept him out most of the season, as his last start prior to his activation in August came back on May 9 — his season was delayed due to left shoulder fatigue. He left his start on Wednesday after just 19 pitches thanks to a groin injury, so his status is currently up in the air.
Snell has made eight total starts this season, six of those coming after he got activated off the injured list again in August. His injuries don’t seem to be lingering as he’s proven to still be one of the best pitchers in the majors.
Across 38.2 innings pitched, Snell owns a 1.86 ERA and 1.09 WHIP while his underlying metrics prove that he’s still the elite pitcher we’ve been used to. His expected numbers look great, supported by an excellent 2.16 xERA and 2.94 xFIP proving that he is more than ready for playoff action.
Snell, a veteran of 11 seasons, has plenty of postseason innings under his belt and has proved at times to be really good when it matters the most.
When I say at times, it is because last season across 13 postseason innings, he struggled with a 6.92 ERA and 1.77 WHIP. On the other hand, he’s accumulated 82.2 total playoff innings in his career, pitching to a respectable 3.27 ERA and 1.15 WHIP between the three teams he’s suited up for.
Keep in mind that Dave Roberts elected to start Snell in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card last year against the Cincinnati Reds, tossing seven quality innings allowing just two runs while striking out seven. Maybe they will go the same direction this year.
Tarik Skubal, LHP
This year’s mid-summer trade deadline was headlined by the fact that Detroit Tigers sensation Tarik Skubal would probably be on the move when it was all said and done. Well, it happened and Skubal found himself as the blockbuster of the deadline, being traded to the Dodgers.
Being named the American League Cy Young in back-to-back seasons with the Tigers in both 2024 and 2025, the Dodgers got one of the best starting pitchers in the majors.
The Dodgers likely would’ve been completely fine without him, but when a team has trade assets like the Dodgers do, it was a no-brainer for them to get a deal done.
Skubal was a solid pitcher from 2020 to 2023, but the last three seasons for him, including this year, have been absolutely phenomenal. Presently in 2026, splitting time between the Tigers and Dodgers, Skubal has logged 146.2 innings spanning 24 starts, while pitching to a 2.70 ERA and 0.95 WHIP.
If the Dodgers decide they want their ace to start Game 1, it’s going to be Skubal. He’s proved way more than he needs to show that he can be a reliable option in the Postseason. On top of his regular season success, Skubal has looked almost better in October.
He totaled 39.2 innings between the 2024 and 2025 postseasons with the Tigers and looked utterly dominant, hence his 2.04 ERA and 0.73 WHIP. Skubal’s 2025 epic performance alone is incredible.
Last year in his American League Wild Card start against the Cleveland Guardians, Skubal tossed 7.2 innings, only allowing one earned run off of three hits, along with a whopping 14 strikeouts.
Subsequently in the Tigers American League Divisional Series against the Seattle Mariners, he made two starts, totaling 13 innings where he allowed only three earned runs, seven total hits, while striking out 22 and issuing just one walk — ace quality numbers for sure.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, RHP
Finally, we have Yamamoto, who might not be getting enough praise that he deserves. He’s in the middle of his third season with the Dodgers and has quietly asserted himself as one of the better starting pitchers in baseball.
The now two-time All-Star finished third in National League Cy Young voting in 2025, and has been incredible thus far in his young career. He’s posted a career ERA of 2.60 so far to go along with a 0.87 WHIP.
This year has been Yamamoto’s best season, and he’s been building off of his 2025 success. Over 27 starts totalling a season-high 179 innings pitched, he’s posted a 2.51 ERA and career-best 0.87 WHIP.
Yamamoto is no stranger to pitching when the lights are the brightest, as he played a massive role contributing to the Dodgers’ World Series title in 2025 against the Toronto Blue Jays. He logged 56 innings of postseason work between 2024 and 2025, resulting in a 2.25 ERA and 0.84 WHIP.
His World Series performance last year was one to remember, tossing 17.2 innings between two starts and a relief appearance with a 1.02 ERA and 0.68 WHIP. In Game 7, he pitched out of relief and closed out the game and series when he got Alejandro Kirk to ground into a double-play.
He’s been an absolute work-horse and should play a huge role this year for the Dodgers in the Postseason, no-matter what role he is given.
The Verdict…
Now onto the final verdict in pinning one of the arms mentioned above to start Game 1 in the playoffs for the Dodgers — a decision that Dave Roberts and his coaching staff won’t take lightly.
The best way to build the Dodgers starting rotation is to alter the handedness each game, so that it’s tougher on whoever their opponent may be. That means with Snell and Skubal both being left-handers and Yamamoto being a right-hander, Yamamoto is best suited to lineup as the Game 2 starter.
As I mentioned previously, the Dodgers did elect to start Snell in Game 1 of the National League Wild Card Series last year, but I do think there will be a change of guard this year.
The Dodgers didn’t go and acquire Skubal to be their Game 3 starter; they acquired him to be their bonafide ace and lead them to another World Series title. It only fits best that he takes the ball for Game 1, meaning Snell would line up best for Game 3.
Skubal, being a two-time Cy Young award winner, two-time All-Star, Triple Crown winner and two-time ERA title winner, indicates that he is more than ready and able to be the Dodgers rotation anchor and leader when October baseball rolls around in a few weeks.

The Los Angeles Dodgers brought third baseman Max Muncy and outfielder Josue De Paula back into the lineup for Thursday’s series finale against the Cincinnati Reds.
The Dodgers lost Wednesday’s game after Cy Young winner Blake Snell went down with a groin injury after pitching just one inning. Luckily, Snell believes he can still make a start before the end of the regular season, which ends in less than two weeks.
LA won the first two games of the series, shutting down a powerful Reds lineup, and will look to do the same to win the series Wednesday.
Who is Starting for the Dodgers?
Justin Wrobleski will start for the Dodgers on Wednesday, making his 25th appearance of the regular season. Two of his last three appearances have come out of the bullpen, and none of them have lasted more than three innings since his return from the injured list with a forearm problem.
He has a 3.78 ERA on the year, striking out 111 batters over the course of 133.1 innings—his heaviest workload in an MLB season so far.
How deep into the game he goes depends on him, but the Dodgers will have backup in the form of Landon Knack whenever Wrobleski is ready to come out.
Who is in the Dodgers’ Lineup?
The Dodgers still don’t have Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but Tommy Edman has replaced him well and will play center field on Thursday. Freddie Freeman moves up a couple of spots into the No. 2 hole, followed by right fielder Kyle Tucker, who will bat third.
Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez takes over the cleanup spot, followed by Muncy, who slides back into third base and bats fifth. De Paula serves as the designated hitter and will bat sixth, with catcher Hunter Feduccia giving Will Smith an off day in the No. 7 spot.
Second baseman Alex Freeland will bat eight for the Dodgers, with Miguel Rojas rounding out the lineup and playing shortstop—giving Mookie Betts a well-deserved rest day.

Who is Starting for the Reds?
Veteran right-hander Brady Singer is starting for the Reds, making his 30th appearance of the season. He has reached that mark in each of the last three seasons, and has 25 or more appearances in all seven of his MLB campaigns bar 2020.
He isn’t having the best year despite his regular consistency, though, as he has a 5.38 ERA through 150.2 innings with only 125 strikeouts on the season.
Singer didn’t face the Dodgers in last week’s series in Los Angeles, but he has a pretty good track record against the team. In three appearances against LA, all of which came during his time with Kansas City, he has a 1.89 ERA through 19 innings with 15 strikeouts.
The Dodgers will hope to break that trend on Thursday as they look to bring themselves even closer to a first-round postseason bye. The first pitch of Thursday’s game comes at 9:40 p.m. PT.

Just when you thought that everything was starting to snap back into place, the Los Angeles Dodgers could be dealing with yet another possible injury. After throwing just one inning against the Cincinnati Reds, Blake Snell was forced to exit the game with left groin tightness. While it is still way too early to hit the nuclear panic button, another Snell injury would pretty much spoil the team's postseason plans.
When it was announced that Shohei Ohtani would no longer pitch for the remainder of the season, the Dodgers were certainly disappointed. But with several strong pitchers already on the road back from injury, they knew that they had options. But with Snell unable to throw more than 19 pitches against the Reds, he may no longer be one of those starting options in the playoffs. That could put the Dodgers in a box that they don’t want to be in.
Could Snell’s early exit have been completely precautionary? Certainly. But it’s still not a good look for a pitcher who has yet to even throw 40 innings in 2026. It’s an especially bad look for the same pitcher who has already been placed on the IL twice this season.
As noted by Dodgers reporter Blake Harris, it’s an even worse look for that very pitcher who suffered a left groin strain just two seasons ago. While pitching for the San Francisco Giants in 2024, Snell was shelved for five weeks for a strain to the same side of the groin he just aggravated in the game against the Reds.
A Blake Snell injury could limit the Dodgers’ World Series run
Again, it’s too early to tell for certain. We might not know the extent of Snell's potential injury for a day or two. However, the most optimistic of recovery timelines would still diminish any chance that Snell has at starting any of the games in the Dodgers’ first postseason series, especially if Snell is dealing with a similar injury to his strained groin.
At 92-59, the Dodgers are in a good position to finish the regular season as one of the top two teams in the National League. That would mean that their first postseason game wouldn’t be until October 3. That would give Snell just two weeks to rest up and treat a potential injury. If he’s looking at anything more than just an acute case of tightness, Snell may even be unavailable for the entire postseason.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow, the Dodgers will have a formidable top three to lead the way. That may be enough to get them through a five-game series in fairly good shape. But if they advance to the NL Championship Series, they will need a fourth starting pitcher.
So what options do the Dodgers have if they need to replace Snell? Emmet Sheehan has looked like an entirely different pitcher over his last two starts. After striking out 10 hitters in 5.2 innings against the Reds on September 7, he backed it up with six scoreless innings against the Miami Marlins in his most recent start. But even with renewed faith in Sheehan, would the Dodgers be comfortable giving him the ball in such a high-stakes series?
Justin Wrobleski has been wildly inconsistent in the second half of the season. With 20 earned runs allowed over his last 20.2 innings pitched, he would likely not be an option for Dodgers manager Dave Roberts. In a perfect world, Kris Bubic would have been the next man up in the rotation, but he will be limited to the bullpen following his own return from the IL.
If the Dodgers are looking at even a modest injury for Snell, their postseason rotation could be their most serious question mark heading into October. They could have enough firepower to cover their weak spot, but it may ultimately be their undoing.

item.content:encoded:
Blake Snell exits Dodgers’ loss early because of injury
- Click here to listen to this article
-
CINCINNATI — The trouble started as Dodgers left-hander Blake Snell threw in the Great American Ball Park bullpen before the game.
“I felt good all day, and then the second-to-last pitch of the bullpen, I threw a slider and then I felt it grab,” Snell said of the groin tightness that ended up taking him out of the Dodgers’ 6-2 loss to the Reds early. “So I was like, ‘Alright, let’s see what we can do.’”
With Snell guiding the ball without driving hard off his back leg, his velocity was down a tick or two through a 19-pitch first inning. He gave up one hit, a single to Sal Stewart, which he quickly erased with a successful pick-off that caught Stewart in an inning-ending run-down.
“I was going to try to get through five [innings],” he said, “but I just knew I didn’t really have a good shot at doing that and remaining healthy.”
In a conversation with manager Dave Roberts, pitching coach Mark Prior and head athletic trainer Thomas Albert, they all agreed the best course of action would be to pull Snell from the game. Right-handed reliever Blake Treinen replaced him in the second inning.
With only 10 games left in the season, it’s unclear when Snell will be ready to pitch again.
“The next couple days are really going to decide,” Snell said. “But I’d love to throw on my next [scheduled start day]. Either there or a couple days after. But definitely, I want to try to get one more in the regular season.”
Teoscar Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday in the Dodgers’ win against the Reds was his second home run in as many nights.
The Dodgers’ loss marked Snell’s eighth start of the season. His 2026 debut was delayed by shoulder fatigue. And then after one start, he landed back on the injured list to undergo arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his left elbow.
Since returning, he hasn’t given up more than one run in a start. Through Wednesday, Snell has a 1.86 ERA. And he’s a key member of the Dodgers’ projected postseason rotation.
“I don’t think anyone can sit here right now and say what’s going to happen in the next week to 10 days,” Roberts said, noting that the team would decide whether to send him to get imaging after they returned to Los Angeles. “It’s under the, ‘I’m glad it’s not worse and we caught it early’ [category].”
Snell has a history of left groin and adductor strains. He spent time on the IL in 2021, 2022 and 2024 for such injuries. He said this injury didn’t feel nearly as severe as any of those.
“[In the past] I felt like that and then I kept pitching on two of them and strained both of them,” he said. “One was a grade one, one was a grade two. So I’m definitely happy I stopped. … I’m aware if I kept pitching, I definitely would’ve strained it. So for me to stop, that’s a first. Maybe I’m growing up. I don’t know. But that was definitely the right move. And next couple days, we’ll see where we’re at and go from there. But I think I’ll be good to go.”
The last couple years, in an effort to avoid another groin strain, Snell has incorporated Copenhagen planks into his routine, strengthening the area.
“I thought I had this thing figured out,” Snell said. “Well, technically, I still do. I didn’t strain it, so that was a good thing. … I haven’t felt it at all until that pitch in the bullpen, and I was just kind of thrown off by it. So I’ve done what I’ve needed to do to be strong and healthy. Definitely a shock to me.”
After Snell left the game, the Dodgers used six relievers to get through seven innings. They combined to give up six runs and 12 hits, including a pair of home runs.
Left-hander Kris Bubic, acquired at the trade deadline while on the IL (flexor strain, shoulder impingement), made his Dodgers debut in the eighth inning. In his first major-league appearance since mid-May, he allowed an infield single and recorded two strikeouts in a scoreless inning.
The Dodgers missed a chance to clinch the division with a win. And the Padres beat the Rockies on Wednesday to keep the division race mathematically alive.
So, the Dodgers will get another shot at champagne showers in Cincinnati Wednesday when left-hander Justin Wrobleski takes the mound. The Dodgers optioned right-hander Bobby Miller after his 2 ⅓ innings Wednesday and plan to recall righty Landon Knack, Roberts said.
The Dodgers’ pitching plans for the next couple weeks are in flux.
Though right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto and left-hander Tarik Skubal have been rounding into the best versions of themselves down the stretch, Snell’s injury is the latest to deplete the ranks.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki (right middle finger blister) has been on the IL for almost three weeks. He threw a four-inning, 48-pitch live batting practice session Wednesday, with Dermabond covering the sensitive area on his finger.
The Dodgers had planned to discuss how to deploy him when he returns from the IL, but after the game, Roberts said to “make sure guys have ample rest,” his next outing will be a start.
Sasaki would be lined up to pitch against the Padres next week.
“It’s playable,” manager Dave Roberts said of Sasaki’s blister. “And given the Dermabond, the time that he’ll have in between this next outing, the hope is that it’s dang near close to being healed.”
Right-hander Tyler Glasnow hit a rough patch in his last two starts but said his back, which sidelined him for three and a half months, “feels good.” The Dodgers sent him back to Los Angeles after the series in Miami to cut down on the number of flights he’d have to sit on before his scheduled start Friday.
“Get him home, get him acclimated to Pacific Standard Time, not have to do two legs,” Roberts said. “So Tyler feels great. He’ll be ready to go on Friday.”
Roberts reiterated after the game that he’s “not concerned with Tyler,” who came out of a bullpen session Wednesday feeling “normal.”
If the Dodgers need another spot start in the next week and a half, they have right-hander Emmet Sheehan waiting in the wings. They optioned him to triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday, in favor of an extra reliever. But over his last two major-league starts, he’s limited opponents to one run and five hits in 11 ⅔ innings.

CINCINNATI — Now what?
Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in four simulated innings to Dodgers hitters on Wednesday afternoon, testing the blister on his right hand that landed him on the injured list. He gave up a home run to Eliezer Alfonzo but otherwise “was good,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Sasaki threw with Dermabond on his injured finger. A surgical adhesive used to close cuts and incisions, pitchers are allowed to use it in games if their team gets permission from MLB in advance.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said. “So we have to huddle up here and figure out what’s his role. What does it look like as we sit here on the 17th or 18th of September, whatever? So the number one most important thing is that he came out of that session well, and then now we got to figure out how to plug him in. He’s going to be important, but I just don’t know right now what role.”
Sasaki seemed destined for a bullpen role again this postseason, a role he assumed successfully last year. But the Dodgers have reason to hesitate on turning Sasaki into a reliever with Blake Snell leaving his start after just one inning on Wednesday night and Tyler Glasnow’s status.
Glasnow flew back to Los Angeles after his start in Miami. It was the second consecutive start in which Glasnow was not sharp and this time he could be seen in the dugout stretching out his back. But after the game, he said his back felt fine and Roberts said Glasnow threw a “normal” bullpen session in L.A. on Wednesday and is scheduled to make his next start on Friday night.
Sasaki is penciled in now to start during the series against the San Diego Padres in Los Angeles next week and remain a starter at least for now.
“One can argue it’s best to take down a couple starts, keep him built up, because if something does happen, he’s built up,” Roberts said. “The other side is you can assimilate him into the ’pen and get comfortable in that role – if that is the role.
“But again, I don’t want to speak out of turn and say that’s done, because it’s not.”
NO SHO
The Dodgers are about to complete their first road trip in three seasons without Shohei Ohtani. Yoshinobu Yamamoto might have missed Ohtani more than any other of his teammates.
“It’s been a weird feeling because I talk to him all the time in the clubhouse,” Yamamoto joked through his interpreter when asked about Ohtani’s absence. “All I have is Roki, but he doesn’t really talk to me.”
Back in Los Angeles, Ohtani has been receiving treatment for his knee and bicep injuries. According to Roberts, Ohtani began swinging a bat, hitting off a tee this week.
“There’s going to be a consistent build-up,” Roberts said. “Don’t know when the time of return to play is, but today was positive, and hopefully we can just keep building towards that.”
Ohtani will be eligible to be activated from the IL next Wednesday. Whether he is ready to play that day or shortly after, Roberts said the expectation is that Ohtani will return in time to play before the regular season ends on Sept. 27.
“I do,” Roberts said. “Whether it happens or not is to be determined. But I do expect him to be back to play in some regular-season games. Don’t know how many of them.”
COMING/GOING
Right-hander Edwin Diaz made his fifth rehab appearance with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless inning to close out the Comets’ playoff berth-clinching victory. Diaz did allow a double to a fellow big-leaguer on rehab, Miguel Andujar.
Meanwhile, Edgardo Henriquez returned to Los Angeles and underwent an MRI, which confirmed the diagnosis of a “low-grade back strain,” Roberts said. He won’t be eligible to pitch again in the regular season but Roberts said the Dodgers are “hopeful” he could come back for the postseason.
Left-hander Kris Bubic was activated from the 60-day IL before Wednesday’s game and right-hander Paul Gervase was returned to OKC. In order to clear a spot on the 40-man roster for Bubic, Triple-A outfielder Ryan Ward was designated for assignment.
Right-hander Landon Knack will be added to the active roster before Thursday’s game and Bobby Miller will be returned to OKC.
ALSO
Outfield prospect Charles Davalan (the 41st pick in last year’s draft) was named MVP of the Class-A Midwest League and Great Lakes manager Jair Fernandez was named the league’s Manager of the Year. Davalan hit .292 with 24 home runs and a .937 OPS. He is scheduled to play in the Arizona Fall League, where he is expected to start testing out a possible conversion to second base.
UP NEXT
Dodgers (LHP Justin Wrobleski, 11-5, 3.78 ERA) at Reds (RHP Brady Singer, 6-14, 5.38 ERA), Thursday, 9:40 a.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers left-handed pitcher Blake Snell has exited Wednesday's game against the Cincinnati Reds after one inning in a concerning development with less than two weeks to go in the regular season.
Snell pitched a scoreless first inning with one strikeout across 19 pitches. There didn't appear to be anything noticeably wrong with him during the frame, but his fastball velocity was down.
At the conclusion of the first inning, Snell went down to the clubhouse alongside team trainer Thomas Albert.
Now, he's out of the game, with right-hander Blake Treinen replacing him in the bottom of the second inning.
What is Blake Snell's Injury?
The Dodgers announced Snell was removed from the game with left groin tightness.
Manager Dave Roberts will provide a more substantial update after the game, which will include whether or not Snell will need to go on the injured list.
Dodgers Can't Afford a Blake Snell Injury Right Now
Snell opened the year on the IL as he recovered from shoulder inflammation that dated back to last year. He returned for one start in May before going right back on the IL to undergo surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
He missed another three months before returning in August, and has been absolutely dominant ever since.
Entering Wednesday, Snell was 4-0 with a 1.04 ERA in six starts since coming off the IL. Including Wednesday's scoreless first inning, he has 47 strikeouts over 35.2 innings and hasn't allowed a home run in that stretch.
The Dodgers are relying on Snell and fellow superstar pitchers Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Tarik Skubal to carry them in October. Thus, the team will hope Snell isn't dealing with anything serious moving forward.
Who Will Replace Blake Snell in Dodgers Rotation if He's Forced to Miss Time?
The Dodgers' starting rotation is dealing with an onslaught of injury concerns as the season winds down.
While the rotation is led by Yamamoto and Skubal (who underwent midseason elbow surgery while with the Detroit Tigers), behind them is a bunch of question marks.
Tyler Glasnow has struggled since returning from a nearly four-month absence due to a back injury. Justin Wrobleski has been removed from the rotation amid his forearm injury and struggles. Roki Sasaki is currently on the IL with a blister. Eric Lauer is out for the season due to an elbow injury.
Then there's Shohei Ohtani, who won't return as a pitcher this year (and may not even be 100% as a hitter).
The Dodgers recently demoted Emmet Sheehan, but could recall him if Snell goes on the IL. He was sharp over his two September starts, allowing one run over 11.2 innings.
If Snell isn't forced to miss time, the Dodgers will take a big sigh of relief knowing their superstar trio in the starting rotation is intact with October looming. If he's forced to go on the IL, though, it will be yet another massive blow in the team's chances to three-peat.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto takes the mound on Tuesday night against the Reds in what figures to be his penultimate start of the regular season. It’s been another fantastic year, once again the anchor of the Dodgers rotation, the only member to stay healthy and make every start this season.
Yamamoto enters Tuesday with 172 innings, only five outs shy of his MLB career high set last year. With two starts left, this year figures to settle into his third-most innings in a season, counting his time pitching for Orix in Japan, with 193 2/3 innings in 2021 and 193 innings in 2022, winning the first two of his three consecutive Eiji Swamura Awards as the best pitcher in Japan.
Unless Justin Wrobleski finds a way to cram 28 2/3 innings into these final 12 games, Yamamoto will once again be the only Dodgers pitcher to qualify for leaderboards, with at least one inning per team game played. Prior to Yamamoto this year and last, no other Dodgers starting pitcher qualified since 2022, when both Julio Urías and Tyler Anderson did so.
Yamamoto this year has the 10th qualifying season by a Dodgers pitcher dating back to 2017, an average of one qualifier per year though going four seasons without (2018, 2020, 2023, 2024) over the last decade. But here’s a fun little quirk: eight of the previous nine Dodgers pitchers to have enough innings to qualify all got Cy Young Award votes in that season.

| Pitcher | Year | Innings | CYA finish | CYA votes |
| Clayton Kershaw | 2017 | 175 | 2nd | 3 1st, 25 2nd, 1 3rd, 1 4th |
| Hyun-jin Ryu | 2019 | 182.7 | 2nd | 1 1st, 10 2nd, 8 3rd, 7 4th, 3 5th |
| Clayton Kershaw | 2019 | 178.3 | 8th | 1 3rd |
| Walker Buehler | 2019 | 182.3 | 9th | 1 4th |
| Walker Buehler | 2021 | 207.7 | 4th | 2 2nd, 9 3rd, 17 4th, 1 5th |
| Julio Urías | 2021 | 185.7 | t-6th | 3 5th |
| Julio Urías | 2022 | 175 | 3rd | 7 2nd, 9 3rd, 5 4th, 1 5th |
| Tyler Anderson | 2022 | 178.7 | n/a | n/a |
| Yoshinobu Yamamoto | 2025 | 173.7 | 3rd | 16 3rd, 11 4th, 2 5th |
| Yoshinobu Yamamoto | 2026 | 172+ | TBD | TBD |
If we extend this back to 2013, 14 of the last 19 Dodgers pitchers to qualify received Cy Young Award votes, thanks to Clayton Kershaw and Zack Greinke each faring well in each of their three seasons as teammates (2013-15).
This season, Jacob Milwaukee Brewers ace Misiorowski is a lock for the National League Cy Young Award, and there is stiff competition with Chris Sale, Cristopher Sánchez, Jesús Luzardo, and others all likely to receive votes as well. But there are five spots on each ballot, and 30 ballots for each league, so “receiving votes” shouldn’t be too high of a bar to clear for Yamamoto this year.
In the list above, Kershaw and Walker Buehler each received a lone vote in 2019, for third and fourth place, respectively, for instance.
Yamamoto entering Tuesday leads the majors in averaging 6.62 innings per start, with his 23 starts lasting at least six inning second-most in the majors, as are his 11 starts of at least seven innings. Yamamoto’s four starts of at least eight innings are tied for most in MLB.
Yamamoto is third in the National League in ERA (2.62) and xERA (3.05), sixth in innings (172), 10th in strikeouts (171), and ninth in strikeout-minus-walk rate (20.1 percent). Yamamoto is also tied for fourth in Baseball Reference WAR (5.4) with Sale, and is tied for fifth in the NL in FanGraphs WAR (4.3) with Reds right-hander Chase Burns.

Wrobleski struck out a batter and allowed two hits and one walk over two scoreless innings of relief in Saturday's 4-3 loss to the Marlins.
After making his previous appearance as a starter Sept. 6 versus the Nationals, Wrobleski shifted back to the bullpen for the Dodgers' weekend series in Miami. He ended up being called upon Saturday in relief of starter Tyler Glasnow, who was chased after yielding four runs across four innings. Assuming the Dodgers elect to maintain a six-man rotation through the end of the season, Wrobleski could have a chance to start or pitch bulk innings again next weekend versus the Giants. The Dodgers reopened a rotation spot after optioning Emmet Sheehan to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
